key_insight: Federated learning across LEO orbital planes, coordinated via HAPS, enables accurate beam selection under rapidly changing propagation while preserving data locality; graph-based models better exploit inter-beam/topology relations than flat MLPs.
problem_solved: Efficient, scalable beam management for LEO Non-Terrestrial Networks under dynamic channel conditions and limited inter-satellite data sharing.
method: Deploy federated learning with orbital planes as clients and HAPS nodes as aggregators to train beam-selection models without centralizing raw channel data.
Compare two local model architectures — a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and a Graph Neural Network (GNN) — on realistic channel and beamforming datasets.
Evaluate beam-selection accuracy, communication overhead, and adaptability to time-varying propagation across federated training rounds.
impact: Demonstrates a practical path to deploy privacy-aware, distributed AI for NTN beam management; highlights that topology-aware GNNs can improve decision quality for spatially coupled wireless tasks while keeping communication costs low.
visual_elements: System diagram: LEO satellites (clients) → HAPS aggregators illustrating federated rounds and local training steps.
Comparison chart: MLP vs GNN — beam-selection accuracy vs communication overhead or adaptability over time.
Map/footprint animation: evolving beam coverage per satellite showing dynamic propagation and selection outcomes.
Flow infographic: data stays local (privacy), model updates aggregated at HAPS, global model redistributed (low-bandwidth arrows).
paper_title: Federated Learning-driven Beam Management in LEO 6G Non-Terrestrial Networks
paper_authors: Maria Lamprini Bartsioka, Ioannis A. Bartsiokas, Athanasios D. Panagopoulos, Dimitra I. Kaklamani, Iakovos S. Venieris
